content.text:
There are two stages. Ingestion resolves declarations into stored funders. PR #52 adds a broader grouping layer for search and funder pages. That second layer is why BBC, GB News and Premier League each appear as one result.

During ingestion, the resolver cleans names and addresses, gets candidate scores from `weldrs`, then applies Rust identity rules. Valid company numbers anchor identities. Exact donor names, extracted name evidence, sufficiently strong name and address matches, and the typed Unite family rule can connect observations. Conflicting company numbers or a person/organisation conflict prevent a merge. The loader persists the resolved identity and its aliases. See [identity rules](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/identity.rs:74) and [funder loading](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs:402).

For the search grouping, the database builds links between stored funders in two ways:

- Their names or aliases match exactly after lowercasing, trimming and collapsing whitespace.
- Their canonical names appear in the same reviewed family table. The table explicitly lists BBC variants, GB News variants and Premier League variants.

These rules live in the [alias migration](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/db/migrations/20261012170746_funder_alias_groups.up.sql:1) and [reviewed family migration](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/db/migrations/20261012173107_reviewed_funder_families.up.sql:1).

The database follows those links transitively. If A shares an alias with B, and B belongs to the same reviewed family as C, all three form one group. The smallest UUID becomes the representative ID, and that funder's stored name becomes the displayed name. There is no automatic substring rule that groups everything containing "BBC".

[Search](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/outbound/funder.rs:37) still scores individual names and aliases. It then keeps the best match per group before applying the result limit. That preserves the relevance of a matching variant while returning one result.

[Funder details](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/outbound/entity_details.rs:105) accept any member ID and collect funding across the whole group. The response includes member IDs and the alias/family links that explain the grouping. Original funder IDs and funding ownership remain intact.

The key caveat is that a reviewed family represents a reporting group. Its members may be separate legal companies. Details therefore omit the company number when members have conflicting numbers. The API exposes the grouping evidence, but the UI does not yet display it.
